about.intro_content: Prof. Xiao-Fei Sun is Professor and Director of the Department of Pediatric Oncology at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, having led the department since 2010.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Sun's research focuses on molecular, prognostic and therapeutic approaches for pediatric cancers including lymphoma, leukemia, brain tumours, neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms tumour, Ewing's sarcoma/PNET and Langerhans cell histiocytosis, with particular expertise in lymphoma diagnosis and treatment using internationally adapted protocols such as modified BFM-90 regimens. She completed visiting fellowships in Japan, Hong Kong and at MD Anderson Cancer Center, USA, and has published more than 60 research papers. She chairs the Pediatric Oncology Committee of the Guangdong Provincial Anti-Cancer Association and is a member of the International Society of Pediatric Oncology (SIOP).

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Xiao-Fei Sun

items.question: Does Prof. Xiao-Fei Sun accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to childhood cancer at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Sun's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Sun specialises in pediatric oncology, including lymphoma, leukemia, neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma and other childhood cancers, with particular depth in lymphoma diagnosis and treatment.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Does Prof. Sun use internationally recognised treatment protocols?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Sun's team adopts international standard treatment strategies, including modified BFM-90 based protocols, for pediatric and adolescent cancer patients.

items.question: Is Prof. Sun involved in clinical trials for pediatric cancer?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Sun has an active interest in pediatric oncology clinical trials and has published extensively on treatment outcomes across multiple childhood cancer types.
